connector: The last day. Yesterday you built your portfolio. Today you present it: one to two minutes, out loud, to a real listener.

a.raw: matthew said it was a girl my girl my girl that im proud of
a.fixed: Matthew said, “It was a girl—my girl—my girl that I’m proud of.”
a.why: Matthew’s real words (Anne of Green Gables, Ch. 36): dashes make the reader pause the way Matthew does.

b.raw: next year i want to read a mystery and keep a reading journal
b.fixed: Next year I want to read a mystery and keep a reading journal.
b.why: Capitals on Next and I; no comma needed (one subject doing two things); a period ends it.

scholar.journal-q3: … and say how you will know you met it.

notes.wgrd: Reflect on how your reading habits have grown: who you were as a reader in August, who you are now, and the proof.
vocab: To change your writing to make the ideas better.
To check writing for mistakes in capitals, usage, punctuation and spelling.
A collection of your best work.
To think back on something and what it taught you.
notes.wordParts: Every base from the year: port, tract, struct, spect, ject, script, rupt, duct, form, press, tain, lev, plus prefixes like pre-, re-, trans-, inter-.
notes.grammar: Spiral review: capitals, commas, quotation marks, complete sentences. Read your sentence out loud and check each mark has a job.
notes.spelling: Spiral review: drop the silent e, change y to i, double the last consonant when the beat is on the last syllable, and spell each word part the same way every time.

transcripts.welcome: Hoo! It’s Opti. The last day of 4th grade ELA. Today you present your portfolio, out loud, to a real listener. Today’s question: if you had two minutes to show someone how you grew, which sentence would you read first?
transcripts.read: Four cue cards. Open with your title and who you were in Week 1. Read one sentence from Piece 1 and one from Piece 3, and say what changed. Share your goal. Then end with your last line. Slow down, and look up.
transcripts.grammar: Your final sentence deserves your best care. Capital at the start. A complete thought. The right mark at the end. Read it out loud. If it sounds like you, it’s ready.
